title: Wanting trumpet, starting clarinet, switching back under Oliver
summary: Told to play clarinet, he learned on a borrowed E-flat from his uncle's band, drifted to soprano sax, then returned to clarinet when Oliver bought him one.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: What was it that inspired you to go into music, Marnie Begard?

Me? Well, I wanted to, truthfully, I wanted to be a trumpet player. Really? And, uh, because, and then I could whistle good. So the, the, the old folks, you know, they said, well, the sun is too much wind. You can't blow that kind of horses. I want to try the clarinet. So, uh, I said, okay. So, uh, I said, okay. So, my uncle was a fiddle player, Emil Begard. A fiddle player? Yeah. He used to lead a band. He used to lead Kid Overs band into that. Uh-huh. And, uh, Baby Daz was the clarinetist. And in those, those days, they used to have a, when they played parade or a funeral, they had what they call a, a, an E-flat clarinet. It was real small, you know. Uh-huh. So, by me being small, my uncle borrowed the clarinet from Baby Daz for me to learn on. And that's how it started. Uh-huh. But I was terrible. Wait. Oh, I was awful. It took me quite a while to get straight. And the only thing that got me straight was, uh, you see, I'd put down the clarinet altogether. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Because at that time, uh, soprano sax was kind of popular. And, uh, the music they were writing, like, they'd have, like, the chorus for sax and then change over to clarinet, well, I'd change over to the soprano. I didn't play the clarinet at all. And we had two good clarinetists in there, Albert Nicholas and Darnell Howard. Uh-huh. So they didn't need me at all on the clarinet. That's the way they went until finally, uh, uh, Nick, Albert Nicholas and Darnell, they went to China. I was supposed to go to China and I didn't want to go. So Oliver says to me, he says, hey, didn't you used to play clarinet? I say, yeah, but forget it. Uh-huh. So he says, no. He says, if I buy you one, will you try to play it? I said, well, I got to lose. I said, sure, go ahead. So he bought me old con clarinet and I started woodshedding. And I found out, I discovered I could play more clarinet than I could in my life. Uh-huh. Because I had the idea from the saxophone, you see. And then it blossomed like that. Then I lost all interest in saxophone. I started with the clarinet and that's how it started all over again.
